title: Affine dictionary for an invertible module and its section
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, X=Spec(R), and M an invertible O_X-module (that is, an O_X-module which is locally free of rank 1) [def-sc-invertible-module]. Put N=Gamma(X,M). Then the canonical counit identifies the quasi-coherent module M [pqf-def-coherent] with the sheaf tilde(N), and N is a finite projective R-module of rank 1 [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] (equivalently, locally free of rank 1 on a finite standard-open cover of Spec(R)). For s in N and p in Spec(R), under the stalk identification M_p=N_p one has s_p in p N_p if and only if s is in pN. Consequently the nonvanishing locus of the section corresponding to s is {p in Spec(R) | s is not in pN}.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas 01IA and 01IB (quasi-coherent sheaves on affine schemes), together with Modules, Lemma 01CY (local criterion for a section of an invertible module)

proof.text: Use IsInvertible.isQuasicoherent and Mathlib isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent to obtain the canonical counit isomorphism.

Apply the existing affine invertible-sections theorem to M and the top affine open. Transport its Module.Invertible structure across ΓSpecIso using localization at the bottom submonoid and the identity module map. Mathlib then supplies Module.Finite and Module.Projective. At a prime, Module.Invertible.of_isLocalization supplies invertibility of the localized module; the local-ring Picard-group instance makes it free, and free_iff_linearEquiv gives N_p ≃ R_p. Apply prime_mem_localized_iff to s for the membership equivalence.

The counit induces a bijective stalk linear map. Compose it with tilde.toStalk to obtain a localization g of N at p.primeCompl, and let e be the canonical localization equivalence. Naturality of the counit (toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app) proves g(s)=germ(s). The stalk ring is R localized at p, so map_eq_maximalIdeal identifies its maximal ideal with the extension of p. Submodule.restrictScalars_map_smul_eq identifies membership in this extended ideal times the stalk with membership in p times the stalk regarded as an R-module, and likewise on the explicit localization. Transport this membership through e using map_smul and e(mk s 1)=g(s). The prime-membership theorem and negation give equality of the two loci by extensionality.

proof_origin.place: Existing affine invertible-sections theorem; canonical tilde stalk localization and scalar restriction of extended ideal products. The original Stacks 01IA/01IB/01CY route is realized with the closed source affine-sections theorem in place of the unfinished standard-cover converse.

lean.statement: theorem affine_cap_section_open_dictionary {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : (Spec (.of R)).Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (s : ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M)) : IsIso (Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓ (R := CommRingCat.of R) M) ∧ (Module.Finite R ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M) ∧ Module.Projective R ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M)) ∧ (∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], Nonempty (((LocalizedModule p.primeCompl ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M)) ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime p] (Localization.AtPrime p))) ∧ (LocalizedModule.mk s 1 ∈ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) p) • (⊤ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M))) ↔ s ∈ p • (⊤ : Submodule R ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M)))) ∧ (nonvanishingLocus M s = {p : PrimeSpectrum R | ¬ s ∈ p.asIdeal • (⊤ : Submodule R ((moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)).obj M))})
